review.title: A Tauri v2 shell that owns the sidecar's lifetime
review.acceptance: A Tauri v2 application starts, spawns the PW-0101 sidecar, reads its bound port from stdout, points the webview at it, and cannot leave the sidecar running. REQUIRED: the Tauri version is pinned exactly, on the rule this repository already applies to Shaka and Playwright -- a caret range means the shell a gate was recorded against can change under a lockfile refresh. REQUIRED: the sidecar is packaged as node.exe plus the standalone tree under bundle.resources and spawned as a child process; pkg, Node SEA and Bun --compile are documented as unable to swallow a Next standalone server and must not be attempted as a shortcut. REQUIRED: a Win32 Job Object with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, because Tauri provides no supervision and an orphaned node.exe holding a loopback port is the failure a user sees as 'it will not start the second time'. REQUIRED: supervision -- health check, restart with a bounded attempt budget, and an honest surfaced failure when the budget is spent, never a blank window. REQUIRED: the shell passes the bearer token to the sidecar through the environment and never on a command line, where it would be readable from the process list. STATED LIMITATION TO CARRY IN THE GATE EVIDENCE: no Windows binary can be produced or run from the cloud session, so this task's build gate is cargo check plus a windows-latest CI job, and 'it launches' is real-device evidence owed to PW-0601.

typecheck.evidence: EXECUTED on 984be77, RE-RECORDED to correct the previous entry, which described a workaround for a problem that did not exist. cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, FULL TREE, no feature flags, exit 0 -- the whole crate including Tauri cross-compiles for Windows. The x86_64-pc-windows-msvc std was installed with rustup; no Windows machine is involved. cargo test --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu 25 passed. Monorepo unchanged: npm run typecheck 21/21, npm run lint 11/11 zero problems, repo:validate passed; this task adds a Rust crate and touches no TypeScript, so those are wrap evidence rather than coverage. WHAT THE PREVIOUS ENTRY GOT WRONG, recorded here because a corrected gate that hides the correction is worse than the error. It reported the full-tree check as blocked inside Tauri's graph and cited three hand-pinned transitive crates. gpt-architect ruled that the top-level version be re-resolved against current stable before concluding the graph was irreconcilable, and that ruling was right: tauri 2.12.0 is the current stable release, not 2.9.1. cargo info in this environment answered 2.9.1 from a STALE LOCAL REGISTRY INDEX, and I took a cache for the registry. The crates.io API returns max_stable_version 2.12.0 for tauri, tauri-runtime and tauri-runtime-wry. Every conflict I pinned around followed from holding a top-level version three minor releases behind its own dependencies -- tauri-runtime 2.12.0 was not too new, it was the version matching a tauri the manifest refused to use. Re-resolved, the tree compiles with ZERO hand-pinned transitive versions and Cargo.lock contains none. The shell cargo feature introduced as a workaround is removed, because leaving it would let --no-default-features produce a binary with no shell. WHAT SURVIVED THE CORRECTION AS REAL EVIDENCE, and gpt-architect ruled it valid: the Windows-target check found that CreateJobObjectW is not exported by windows-sys without the Win32_Security feature, because SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES appears in its signature. That was found by cross-checking for Windows from Linux and by nothing else.

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on 96cdb0e. cargo test --manifest-path apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -> 25 passed, 0 failed, exit 0. The monorepo suite is unchanged at 20/20 with apps/web at 1109; this task adds no TypeScript. WHAT THE 25 DEFEND, and the ones that matter are ABSENCES rather than behaviours. THE TOKEN IS ASSERTED NOT TO APPEAR IN ANY ARGUMENT: launch_arguments is built from a planned launch whose token is a real 64-character value, and every argument is asserted not to contain it while the environment IS asserted to carry it. That is the PW-0101 property from the other side -- a Windows process's command line is readable by any process running as the same user and is shown in Task Manager, so argv would publish the one value separating our listener from every other local process. NO FAILURE REPORT MAY CONTAIN THE TOKEN: all six startup failures are described and scanned, and the Token arm is deliberately CONSTRUCTED with the token embedded in its inner message so that forwarding that message would fail the test -- the arm drops it and says so. A NON-LOOPBACK HANDSHAKE HOST IS REFUSED: 0.0.0.0, a LAN address, a domain and localhost are each refused, and this is a RESTATEMENT of a rule apps/web/src/lib/sidecar/handshake.ts already enforces, not an inheritance of it. The justification is in the module: this process is the one that acts on the value by pointing a webview at it, and a compromised or simply buggy child is exactly the case where the producer's check did not run, so a consumer that trusted the producer would be trusting the thing it validates. AN UNUSABLE PORT IS REFUSED RATHER THAN WRAPPED: 0, -1, 70000, 65536, a string and null. 70000 narrowed to u16 is 4464, a perfectly plausible port, which is why the range check precedes the narrowing. IPv6 IS BRACKETED: http://::1:41999/ is not a URL and the shell would silently fail to navigate. ORDINARY LOG LINES ARE NOT ERRORS while a handshake-shaped line with no body IS -- the caller reads every line the child prints, so collapsing those two would either report a broken contract on Next's startup banner or swallow a genuinely broken one. THE RESTART BUDGET: four consecutive failures then a stated failure, never an unbounded loop behind a blank window; a healthy run clears the budget BEFORE its own failure is charged, so a crash after an hour is a first failure rather than a fifth; the boundary at MIN_HEALTHY_RUN minus one millisecond is asserted, because roughly twenty seconds is not a rule; the backoff shift is asserted not to overflow at u32::MAX, because 1 << attempt is undefined past 63 and the input is a counter; and the worst-case total wait before the user is told something is asserted under fifteen seconds, because that total is what a person actually experiences. THE LAUNCH PLAN: a short or non-hex token is refused before anything is spawned, since this process MINTS it and learning at the sidecar's bind check that the shell generated rubbish would put the failure in the wrong half of the system; a missing runtime names what is missing and where, because an incomplete-installation message with no path is a support ticket nobody can act on; and resources are asserted to resolve under the directory given rather than the current one, which is the difference between working under cargo run and failing in an installed build. FIVE TESTS ARE WINDOWS-BEHAVIOUR-SHAPED AND ARE NOT CLAIMED AS SUCH: job.rs's tests assert the error text names which step failed, and that a non-Windows build REFUSES rather than silently running unsupervised. Whether the kernel terminates job members is not asserted by anything here and cannot be from this environment.

build.evidence: RE-RECORDED on 984be77, still FAIL, and the reason is now narrower and truer than the previous entry's. gpt-architect ruled the build gate must remain FAIL because the acceptance defines it as cargo check PLUS windows-latest CI evidence, and that partial evidence must not be relabelled as a passed build gate. HALF ONE NOW PASSES: cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc over the full tree, exit 0, no feature flags and no hand-pinned transitive versions. The previous entry reported this half as blocked inside Tauri's graph; that was wrong, and the cause was mine -- cargo info answered from a stale local registry index and I concluded tauri 2.9.1 was the current stable when 2.12.0 is. ADR-009 keeps the whole episode rather than being rewritten, per the ruling. HALF TWO DOES NOT EXIST: there is no windows-latest CI job. .github/workflows/windows.yml belongs to PW-0501, which gpt-architect confirmed in round 87 as the owner of the Windows build runner, and PW-0501 depends on PW-0102 so the ordering is already enforced. No artifact has been built, nothing has launched, WebView2 has rendered nothing, no Job Object has terminated anything and no installer has run. THIS GATE IS THE PLACE WHERE THAT DISTINCTION IS HELD. Compilation evidence is not build evidence, and a cross-compile check that never links is not even a build. It should stay FAIL until PW-0501's runner produces an artifact, and PW-0102 must not reach DONE before then.

recommended.title: The authenticated backend the desktop build talks to
recommended.acceptance: The counterparty the desktop forwarder already speaks to exists as a service instead of only as an e2e stub. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 was ruled by the commander: provider resolution must not rely on the user-administered sidecar as its trust boundary, and the desktop build proxies to an authenticated backend. The FORWARDER is implemented and tested; the thing it forwards TO is e2e/src/backend-stub.mjs. REQUIRED: the same route contract, byte for byte -- the cross-target e2e suite already compares whole bodies between targets and must keep passing. REQUIRED: caller authentication, and a refusal that does not leak whether a content id exists. REQUIRED: provider credentials live only here, never in a desktop artifact, env var, config file or cached response; the build-target import-graph guard already proves the desktop bundle cannot reach @liberty/provider-sdk and this service is where that capability actually lives. REQUIRED: it is deployable and testable WITHOUT a licensed provider -- the resolution path must return an honest unavailable with provider_not_configured when none is wired, which is exactly what the web target already does. THIS TASK DOES NOT NEED CREDENTIALS and must not wait for them; PL-0302 remains the separate task that wires a real provider into it.
